featuresTitle:
The details you need.
An interface that gets out of the way.
featureSearchText: Search repositories and tags, navigate namespaces, and jump straight into the image you need.
featureLayersText: Inspect multi-platform manifests, image configuration, compressed layers, history and OCI metadata.
featureOwnText: Two interface languages (English and German), System/Light/Dark and configurable branding.
featureAuthText: Use anonymous access or native Basic Auth. Credentials stay in an encrypted, HttpOnly session cookie.
featureNativeText: Works with Registry HTTP API V2, OCI image indexes and the standard referrers tag fallback. No separate search service.
featureControlText: Manifest deletion is opt-in. The confirmation shows every tag affected by deleting the digest.
installTitle:
A small addition to
your existing stack.
installDescription: Start with the complete Docker Compose stack, or connect Crateview to a registry you already run.
honestTitle: A UI for your registry. Clear about its boundaries.
honestText: Crateview shows what the registry actually provides. Image creation dates are not push timestamps. Compressed image sizes are not registry disk usage. Scanning and user administration stay with dedicated services.
faq1a: No. It runs alongside your registry. The registry stores images and controls access; Crateview provides the web interface and a same-origin proxy.
faq2a: Anonymous access and native htpasswd Basic Auth are supported. External Bearer-token services and OIDC are unsupported. User administration is not available in this release.
faq3q: Can I use my own branding?
faq3a: Yes. Set the app name, logos, favicon, links and theme defaults through environment variables. Further component styling uses standard Nuxt UI configuration.
faq4q: Does deleting a tag remove just that tag?
faq4a: Standard manifest deletion works by digest and affects every tag pointing to it. It is disabled in the UI by default and requires explicit configuration in both Crateview and the registry.

faqPwaQuestion: Can I install Crateview as an app?
faqPwaUpcoming: PWA support is coming in {version}; it is not included in the currently documented stable release.
faqPwaAvailable: Yes. PWA support is available in the documented stable release.
faqPwaDetails: Use a supported browser’s install or Add to Home Screen action over HTTPS (localhost works for local tests). After an online visit installs the service worker, offline starts show a localized retry screen. Registry browsing and account actions still need the network; their responses are not stored for offline use. The app name and separate 192- and 512-pixel PNG icons are configurable. Test with a production build.
